what: DERIVATION, independent attempt 3 of 3: What do the axioms say about the past of a record?. A READING task with a strict rule: read the COMPLETE axioms text on main before writing anything (docs/MINIMAL_AXIOMS_2026-06-29.md and every note it cites as axiom-level; never truncate; quote with file and line). The probes found that the physics depends on the predecessor structure of a record: with a backward past on Z^3 (2+1) a continuous menu forgets and there is no three-dimensional potential; with a past that has three-dimensional level planes (3+1) memory survives and the equal-time kernel is a Green function; with a SYMMETRIC light-cone past the static response to a persistent source is exactly the lattice Green function. TASK: (a) extract every sentence of the axioms and of the causal-time lane on main that constrains which records a new record is formed from (its past), whether records are permanent, whether time is a lattice direction or derived ('one clock', '3+1', 'anomaly forces time'), and the role of Z^3; (b) list the predecessor structures consistent with those sentences, and those excluded, each with the sentence that decides; (c) if the text does not decide, say exactly which clause would have to be added and what it would cost (the axiom-update criterion of the repository asks for a layman-simple insight). No physics verdict; a map with citations. check.py verifies that every quoted line exists at the cited path and line on origin/main. ROUND 2: the first round's attempts and referee reports are under probes/work/derive/<problem>/ and logs/probes/J:derive:*/ and logs/probes/J:confirm:J-derive-*/ (python3 probes/harvest.py lists them); what survived refereeing is stated below as GIVEN, what failed is stated as the gap. DELIVERABLE, in your unit worktree on ai/probes: probes/work/derive/axioms-and-the-event-lattice/<your worker name>/ATTEMPT.md and check.py. ATTEMPT.md: (1) the exact statement you attempt; (2) numbered steps, each marked PROVED (argument given in full), CHECKED (a finite fact check.py verifies exactly) or ASSUMED; (3) if the route fails, the FIRST step that fails and why: a precise no-go for a route is a result; (4) what would finish it. check.py: exact arithmetic (fractions, integers, sympy) for every finite claim; it prints `SUMMARY: PROVED ...`, `SUMMARY: COUNTEREXAMPLE ...`, `SUMMARY: PARTIAL <what is new and exact>` or `SUMMARY: ROUTE FAILS AT <step>`, and a line `HIT: <the claim>` ONLY when you claim a proof, a counterexample, or a new exact partial result others can build on; a HIT is handed to a worker of another model family to referee line by line, so write for a hostile reader. Rules: definitions come from the notes on the PR branches named above (git fetch origin <branch>; git show origin/<branch>:<note>; find them with gh pr view <n> --json files,headRefName); any outside theorem you use must be re-proved at the scope you use it or listed under ASSUMED; no status words (proved theorems are promoted by the supervisor after the referee). Have your own plan BEFORE reading the prior attempts printed at claim time; then either build on a refereed partial result or take a different route. Run: python3 probes/run_probe.py <task> --worker <name> --model <model> --review "..." --extra "python3 probes/work/derive/axioms-and-the-event-lattice/<name>/check.py"
